views.doc:
Start page of the ShuttleBuilder: explains what a Shuttle is and how to install one.

- Static help text; no data is shown or changed. No login required.
- Describes the workflow: create a Shuttle in `<shuttle-instance-list>`, download the executable, install it on the lab PC.
- Contains install steps for Windows, Windows XP with SFTP and Linux (systemd), with links to the needed helper files.
- Links to `<shuttle-scripts>` for preprocess scripts, the OpenAPI file and the Chemotion documentation.

headings: List of all liked GIT repos
views.doc:
List of all linked git repositories (`GitInstance`) with Shuttle source code; the active one is marked `ACTIVE`.

- "Activate" (inactive repos) clones the repo and makes it the only active one; Shuttles are then built from it.
- "Reload" (active repo) clones it again to pick up new commits.
- Both run on the server and can take a while; a loading screen is shown. All Shuttles are rebuilt on their next download.
- "NEW" opens `<git-insatnce-edit>` to link a repo; the wrench edits one; the trash button deletes it after a confirm dialog.
- Requires login.

Lists, creates and revokes the API tokens of the logged-in user: tokens let programs and AI assistants use the
site with the user's account through the REST API (`sdc_api/`) or MCP.

- No arguments; login required.
- The list shows every token of the user (also expired and revoked ones): name, the first characters of the
  token, privileges, creation, expiry and last use. Tokens of `sdc_api/login/` (username and password) are
  marked "login".
- "Create token" needs a name, a lifetime ("Valid for") and privileges: "Read only" (read all data and the
  account), "Read & write" (also create and change data), "Full access" (also delete data, change the profile
  and manage tokens) or "Custom" (read/write/delete per data model or for all of them, and the account
  privileges). A token never has more rights than the user.
- The new token is shown once above the list with a "Copy" button; it cannot be shown again.
- "Revoke" asks for confirmation and then revokes the token and every token created with it; this cannot be
  undone.

actions.copy_token: Copies the new token to the clipboard.
actions.revoke_token:
Revokes the token of the button (`data-token-id`) after a confirmation; tokens created with it are revoked
as well.
actions.create_token: Creates a token with the entered name, lifetime and privileges and shows it once; the list is reloaded.

views.doc:
Login form (username and password) that starts a session for an `SdcUser`; the view other views redirect to when login is required.

- Arguments: `next` (optional) is the URL to go to after login; without it the project's start page (`LOGIN_SUCCESS`) is used.
- "Login" checks the credentials. On success the user is logged in and the whole page reloads at the `next` target; on failure the errors are shown in the form.
- If the project requires confirmed e-mail addresses and the user has not confirmed theirs, login is refused and a new confirmation e-mail is sent.
- Links lead to `<sdc-password-forgotten>` and to `<register>`.

List of the user's Shuttle instances (staff see all), with search, download and management actions.

- Download builds the executable for that instance from the active git repo and downloads it; this may take a while.
  Result: the bare executable, a ZIP with WinSCP (Windows i386 + SFTP), or a ZIP with ChemConverter and the profile (with converter).
- The wrench opens `<shuttle-instance-edit>` for the instance; "Copy" opens it prefilled as a new copy.
- The trash button deletes the instance and its build files after a confirm dialog; this cannot be undone.
- "NEW" opens `<shuttle-instance-edit>` to create one.
- Shows the active git repo; if none is linked the list is not shown. Requires login.

Help page about preprocess scripts that a Shuttle runs on each file before sending it.

- Static text; no data is shown or changed. Requires login.
- Explains the script folder (`~/shuttle/scripts` on Linux, `%USERPROFILE%\shuttle\scripts` on Windows) and how scripts are run.
- Offers downloads of the "ShuttleFromContentRenamer" script and of the ChemConverterApp (Linux and Windows).
- The ChemConverter is not a script; it is enabled with `with_converter` in `<shuttle-instance-edit>`.

Form to link a new git repository or edit an existing `GitInstance`.

- Arguments: `pk` (optional) is the id of the repo to edit; without it a new repo is created.
- New repo: "Save & Done" creates it and returns to `<git-instance-list>`. It is not active until activated there.
- Edit: there is no save button; changes are stored by the model form directly.
- The `name` cannot be changed after creation. Changing `url` or `branch` takes effect on the next reload/activation.
- Requires login.

Registration form that creates a new `SdcUser` account; open it from the "Register" link of `<sdc-login>` or `<sdc-user-nav-btn>`.

- Arguments: `model` must be `SdcUser`; `next` is where to go after creating (the links pass `..`, i.e. back).
- Fields: `username`, `first_name`, `last_name`, `email`, the password and its confirmation (must match and pass the password rules).
- "Create" creates the account; anyone may register, no login is needed. The new user is not logged in automatically.
- If an `email` was given, a confirmation e-mail with a link to `<sdc-confirm-email>` (valid 3 days) is sent to it.
- If the project requires confirmed e-mail addresses, the new user can only log in after following that link.

tasks.title: Register a new account
steps: Fill `username`, `password1` and `password2` (the user types the passwords) and optionally the names and `email`.
The user clicks "Create"; with an `email` a confirmation e-mail is sent.

views.doc:
Generic read-only view of one record of an SDC model, rendered with the model's detail template.

- Arguments: `model` (required) is the SDC model name and `pk` (or `id`) the record id, e.g. `/~sdc-detail-view~&model=Author&pk=3`.
- The view refreshes automatically when the record changes on the server.
- Usually reached via the "Detail" link of a `<sdc-list-view>` row; access depends on the model's server-side permissions.

Generic live list of the records of one SDC model, rendered with the model's list template.

- Arguments: `model` (required) is the SDC model name, e.g. `/~sdc-list-view~&model=Author`; optional `filter` restricts the records (normally only set from code by a parent view).
- The list updates automatically when records are created, changed or deleted (model socket).
- An embedded `<sdc-search-view>` (if the model's list template has one) filters and pages the list.
- In the default list template each row has "Edit" (opens `<sdc-model-form>`), "Detail" (opens `<sdc-detail-view>`) and "Remove"; "Remove" asks for confirmation in a dialog and then deletes the record on the server; this cannot be undone.
- What is listed and whether delete is allowed is decided by the model's server-side permissions.

actions.removeInstance: Deletes the record of the "Remove" button (`data-instance-pk`) of the list's model. This cannot be undone.

views.doc:
Requests a password-reset e-mail for a user who forgot their password; reached from the "Password forgotten" link of `<sdc-login>`.

- No arguments and no login needed. Enter the username or the e-mail address of the account.
- "Send E-mail" sends an e-mail with a link to `<sdc-reset-password>` to the account's address; the link is valid for 3 days and can be used once.
- An empty input only shows a hint, no request is sent.
- Shows "User not found" if no account (or more than one) matches, and an error if the e-mail could not be sent.

actions.send_email:
Sends a password reset e-mail to the user with the entered username or e-mail address; shows an error
message if the field is empty.

views.doc:
Generic create/edit form for one record of an SDC model, generated from the model's server-side form; saves via the model socket.

- Arguments: `model` (required) is the SDC model name; with `pk` (or `id`) it edits that record, without it it creates a new one (e.g. `/~sdc-model-form~&model=Author&pk=3`).
- Edit mode: every field change is saved automatically, there is no save step; with `form_name=<name>` a named alternative form of the model is used, and with `auto_save=false` changes are only stored when the save button (`button_text`, default "Save") is pressed.
- Create mode: "Create" creates the record and then navigates to `next` (default `..`, one level up); `reset_on_save=true` instead clears the form for another entry, `editing_after_save=true` switches to editing the new record.
- After a successful save of an existing record the form navigates to `next` if given.
- Other optional arguments: `form_header` (heading text) and `filter` (selects the record to edit instead of `pk`).
- Validation errors are shown at the fields; who may create or edit is decided by the model's server-side permissions.
- Also used as a mixin by app-specific form controllers.

Form to create, edit or copy a `ShuttleInstance` (the configuration of one Shuttle executable).

- Arguments: `pk` (optional) is the id of the instance to edit; `copypk` (optional) prefills a new instance from an existing one, with ` (COPY)` added to the name.
- Without `pk`: "Save & Done" creates the instance (owned by the current user) and returns to `<shuttle-instance-list>`.
- With `pk`: there is no save button; changes are stored by the model form directly.
- The `common_name_parts` field is only shown for type `flat_tar`; it has a test input that shows the regex match and structure.
- The BagIt fields (`dst_bagit`, `user_bagit`, `passwort_bagit`, `profile`, `public_link`) are only shown when `with_converter` is checked.
- `host_key` is only shown for SFTP and `cert` only for WebDAV and ChemAssistent; `insecure` always shows a red warning (translated notes come from the template).
- For the transfer type `chemassistent` the `password` label becomes "API key (cam_...)", `user`, `host_key` and the converter block are hidden,
  and `dst` is pre-filled with the ChemAssistentManager URL (if configured) next to a link to create a job and an API key.
  For `win_i386` a hint says that Windows XP speaks at most TLS 1.2. Switching back restores the WebDAV/SFTP view.
- Shows the active git repo; if none is linked the form is not shown. Requires login.

embedded.doc:
Logout button; usually embedded in `<sdc-user-nav-btn>` when a user is logged in.

- "Logout" ends the session of the current user immediately (no confirm dialog) and redirects to the login view; the WebSocket connections are reopened as anonymous user.

Root navigation frame of an SDC app: owns the URL, the nested views and the breadcrumb; there is one per page and it is exposed as `window.sdcNav`.

- URL scheme: `/~<tag>~<child-tag>~&key=value&...`. Each `~` segment is a controller tag rendered nested inside the previous one; arguments after `~&` are passed to the views as data attributes (`N.key=value` targets only the view at depth `N`, plain `key` applies to the deepest one). Relative paths (`.`, `..`, `*` = keep the current segment at that depth) are resolved against the current path.
- An empty path opens the controller named in its `default-controller` argument; a view container with its own `data-default-controller` opens that child automatically.
- Links with the class `navigation-links` are handled client-side without page reload; `window.sdcNav.goTo('<path>', {args})` (or triggering the `goTo` event) navigates programmatically. Browser back/forward works.
- An unknown tag in the path shows `sdc-error 404` instead of the view. A view whose `allowedPaths` do not match the views in front of it shows `sdc-error 403` ("Not allowed"), e.g. `/~settings` for a view only allowed below `dashboard`. Some containers open their view in a modal; closing the modal navigates back one level.
- Links marked as login-only/logout-only are shown or hidden depending on whether a user is logged in; the `login`/`logout` events reload the whole page.

Search and paging bar embedded at the top of a model list (inside `<sdc-list-view>`); its fields come from the model's server-side search form.

Changing a search field filters the surrounding list immediately (no submit button needed). "Prev"/"Next" page through the results and the bar shows the current range and total count; the paging controls are hidden when everything fits on one page. It changes no data.
embedded.summary: Search and paging bar of a model list; changing a field filters the list at once.

unreached.doc:
Chat panel of the AI assistant, fixed at the right edge of the page; only rendered when the project sets `SDC_AI_ASSISTANT`.

- The user types a question; the answer streams in. The assistant can also act on the page, always with the
  logged-in user's permissions: open views like a navigation link, read the current page, enter values into
  its forms (also the search bar of `<sdc-search-view>`, which filters its list at once), click buttons and
  links, and read SdcModel records.
- The assistant never submits a form: it fills forms (SdcModel forms are marked by `SdcModelName` /
  `SdcModelPK`) like the user, so auto-saving edit forms save the values at once; new records are only created
  when the user submits. After every change the chat shows "Restore", which sets the previous values back.
  Before it clicks a button that may delete, save or send data or log out, the chat asks the user to allow it. Links that leave the app are not clicked. It
  never reads or fills password, hidden or file fields.
- Depending on the project settings it requires a login, and either uses the server's API key or the user's own.
- "⚙" opens the settings: with the server's key they only show the model in use; otherwise the user enters their
  API key and may choose the provider (Anthropic or any OpenAI-compatible API such as the KIT KI-Toolbox) and set
  the API URL (https, public hosts only), model, effort and max tokens. Changing the provider starts a new
  conversation. "Remember on this device" keeps the settings in the browser, the key only until the tab is closed.
- The panel starts collapsed at the right edge of the page; a click on it (or "⇆") expands it, "⇆" collapses it
  again. It opens by itself when the settings need the user's API key.
- Esc while the panel is open stops a running answer (its model request and remaining actions) and collapses
  the panel; the conversation goes on with the next prompt.
- Dragging the header moves the panel and dragging its edges or corners resizes it (kept in the browser);
  a double-click on the header docks it at the right edge again.

Global toast area for status messages; usually placed once in the page next to `<sdc-navigator>`.

Messages pushed by other controllers (e.g. success or validation errors after a form submit) appear here with a header and time and disappear automatically after about 2 seconds; error messages are highlighted. Nothing to operate.

Form for the logged-in user to change their own password (the `password_form` of `SdcUser`).

- No arguments; it always edits the current user. Requires login, otherwise it redirects to the login view.
- Enter the current password, then the new password twice (must match and pass the password rules).
- "Change password" saves the new password immediately. Other sessions of this user are logged out; the current session stays logged in.

Confirms the e-mail address of an `SdcUser`; this is the target of the link in the confirmation e-mail.

- Arguments: `token` (required) is the token from the e-mail link (`/~sdc-confirm-email~&1.token=...`).
- Opening the view with a valid token immediately marks the address as confirmed (`email_confirmed`) and shows a success message; there is nothing to click. No login is needed.
- Each token works once and is valid for 3 days. An expired token automatically sends a new confirmation e-mail; an invalid or already used token shows "No valid token.".
Placeholder/test view that shows the text of its `text` argument (e.g. `/~sdc-dummy~&text=Hello`) followed by any content placed inside the tag. Has no actions.

Error page that shows "We have an error: <code>" for the HTTP status in its `code` argument.

- `<sdc-navigator>` shows `sdc-error 404` when a path segment names an unknown controller.
- `sdc-error 403` (or similar) means the server refused the view: log in, or use a user with the required permissions.
- It has no actions; navigate elsewhere (link, breadcrumb, browser back) to leave it.

Sets a new password with a reset token; this is the target of the link in the password-reset e-mail sent by `<sdc-password-forgotten>`.

- Arguments: `token` (required) is the token from the e-mail link (`/~sdc-reset-password~&1.token=...`); it is kept in a hidden form field.
- Enter the new password twice (at least 8 characters, must match and pass the password rules). No login is needed.
- "Reset Password" sets the new password and shows "Password has been reset."; the user is not logged in and must then use `<sdc-login>`.
- Each token works once and is valid for 3 days. An expired token automatically sends a new reset e-mail; an invalid or used token shows an error.

Searchable dropdown that replaces a normal select field inside forms (rendered by the `SearchableSelect` form widget); the selected value(s) are submitted under the field's name.

Click it to open the option list, type to filter (space or comma separated terms, all must match), click an option to select it. With multiple selection each selected value has a "×" button to remove it; the same applies to single selection when the field is not required. Each change fires a change event, so inside an edit-mode `<sdc-model-form>` it is saved immediately.

actions.onDeactivate: Closes the option list when the user clicks beside it; the selection stays unchanged.
actions.onActivate: Opens the option list with its filter field.
actions.remove_selection:
Removes the clicked value ("×") from the selection and fires a change event; inside an edit-mode
`<sdc-model-form>` the record is saved at once.

unreached.summary: Searchable dropdown that replaces a select field in forms.

unreached.doc: Invisible global helper that loads the `SdcUser` record of the logged-in user (nothing for anonymous visitors) and provides it to other controllers on request; it shows no content and has no actions.

User area for the navigation bar: shows "Login" and "Register" links when nobody is logged in, and an "Edit <username>" link (opens the user's own `SdcUser` in `<sdc-model-form>`) an "API tokens" link (opens `<sdc-api-tokens>`) and `<sdc-logout>` when a user is logged in. It refreshes itself after login and logout.

Login page; wraps the standard `<sdc-login>` form.

- Users can log in with a local account or, if a Chemotion ELN is connected, with their Chemotion username and password.
- With an active `ElnConnection` the page shows a link to that Chemotion server.
- A Chemotion login creates or updates a local account with the same name; new accounts of Chemotion admins become staff.
- No login required.

models.name: ElnConnection
models.doc:
Connection to a Chemotion ELN server whose accounts may log in to the ShuttleBuilder.

- `url`: base URL of the Chemotion instance; `active`: only the active connection is used for login.
- `token`, `device`: optional Chemotion API token and device id for this connection.
- If no connection is active and the setting `ELN_URL` exists, an active connection to it is created automatically.
- Users who log in with Chemotion credentials get a local account; new ones become staff if they are Chemotion admins.
- Managed in the Django admin (`/admin/main_app/elnconnection/`); saving one as active deactivates all others.
- `<shuttle-login>` shows the active connection's URL.

models.name: ElnUser
models.doc:
Per-user profile that records whether a user logs in through the connected Chemotion ELN.

- One record per Django `User` (`user`, one-to-one); created automatically when a user is created.
- `is_eln_user`: `true` if the last login was verified by the active `ElnConnection`, `false` for a local account login.
- `token`: Chemotion API token from the last ELN login; empty for local logins.
- Both fields are set by the login process, not by the user.
- Each user can only read their own record; deleting the `User` deletes it.

models.name: GitInstance
models.doc:
A git repository (and branch or commit) holding the Shuttle source code that executables are built from.

- `name`: unique, cannot be changed later; `url`: clone URL; `branch`: branch name or commit id (default `main`).
- `is_active`: exactly one repo is active; all Shuttle builds use it. Activating a repo makes it the source of every later build.
- `last_reload`: when the repo was last cloned (`git clone`, then `git checkout <branch>`); `null` means it is cloned on the next build. A failed clone or checkout raises an error and keeps the previous checkout.
- `shuttle_version`: version of the Shuttle in the checkout (`shuttleVersion` in `main.go`), read after every successful reload; empty if it cannot be found. Shown in the git list (`<git-instance-list>`), also as the version a download will build (tooltip of the download button in the Shuttle list).
- If none is active, the default `ComPlat/shuttle/Main` (https://github.com/ComPlat/shuttle.git, `main`) is created and activated.
- Rolling out a new Shuttle version: reload the active repo (or activate another one). Afterwards every `ShuttleInstance` is rebuilt on its next download (its `built_version` then shows the new version); the lab downloads the Shuttle again, replaces the executable and restarts it. Already installed Shuttles are not updated by themselves.
- Builds use the toolchains of the server image: Go 1.26.11, and Go 1.10.8 (`XP_GOROOT`) for Windows i386 (Windows XP).
- Readable and editable by every logged-in user.
- Listed and activated in `<git-instance-list>`, created/edited in `<git-insatnce-edit>`.

models.name: ShuttleInstance
models.doc:
Configuration of one Shuttle: a small program for a lab PC that watches a folder and uploads new data (WebDAV, SFTP or an HTTP upload to a ChemAssistentManager job).

Fields:
- `name`: unique, cannot be changed later; also the name of the working folder `~/shuttle/shuttle_<name>/` on the lab PC. `owner`: the creating user. Logged-in users see and change only their own instances; staff and superusers see all.
- `src`: folder to watch on the lab PC (entered plainly, no doubled backslashes); `duration`: seconds a file must stay unchanged before it is sent (default 300, at least 1; it is also the longest wait between retries).
- `transfer`: `webdav`, `sftp` or `chemassistent`; `dst`, `user`, `password`: target URL and credentials on the server. `dst` is checked: SFTP `host[:port]/path` (also `ssh://` or `sftp://`, port 22 by default), WebDAV `http(s)://host/path`.
- `chemassistent`: Shuttle uploads by HTTP POST to a ChemAssistentManager job (trigger "HTTP file upload (API key)"); one upload starts one AI run. `password` holds the API key (`cam_...`, 20 to 200 characters, created once in ChemAssistentManager; a key without the `cam_` prefix is rejected); `user` is not used (it is cleared). `dst` is `http(s)://host` of the ChemAssistentManager server (an empty path or `/` becomes `/api/jobs/trigger`) or the full trigger URL of the job. `with_converter` and `host_key` do not apply. `cert` and `insecure` work as for WebDAV. Per `shuttle_type`: `file` and `flat_tar` = one run per file, `folder` = one run per folder (nested names are flattened, `A/B/x.csv` becomes `A__B__x.csv`), `zip` / `tar` = one run per archive. At most 100 MB per upload (Shuttle default, not configurable here). A local file is deleted only after the server accepted it (HTTP 202); with a revoked key or a disabled job the files stay and wait for a rebuilt Shuttle with a new key. Built for every architecture; Windows XP speaks at most TLS 1.2, so the server must offer TLS 1.2.
- `shuttle_type`: `file` (each file), `folder` (whole folder once complete), `zip` / `tar` (folder as an archive once complete) or `flat_tar` (files grouped by the `common_name_parts` regex into .tar.gz archives). A changed folder is sent again completely.
- `architecture`: target system: `win_i386` (also Windows XP), `win_64`, `ubuntu_64`, `raspberry_pi_6`, `raspberry_pi_7` or `raspberry_pi_64`. Windows i386 is built with Go 1.10.8, everything else with Go 1.26.11.
- `with_converter`: also convert data with ChemConverterApp to a BagIt archive, sent to `dst_bagit` with `user_bagit`/`passwort_bagit`; needs a JSON `profile`, `public_link` is the URL prefix of the raw files. The converter ships in the zip (Windows x64, Linux); a failing conversion is skipped and the raw data is still sent.
- `host_key` (SFTP only): expected SSH host key fingerprint of the server, `SHA256:<base64>` (optionally `ssh-ed25519 255 SHA256:...` as shown by WinSCP) or MD5 `aa:bb:...`. It applies to both SFTP destinations, so with a converter both must be the same server. Required for `win_i386` + SFTP unless `insecure` is set. Otherwise empty means trust on first use: Shuttle stores the key of the first connection in `known_hosts` and refuses a changed key later.
- `cert` (WebDAV and ChemAssistent only): PEM server certificate (`.crt`, `.pem`, `.cer`), needed for self-signed servers and the only way TLS is verified on Windows XP. It is built in as `server.crt` and shipped next to the executable (the download becomes a zip).
- `insecure`: WARNING, disables TLS certificate **and** SSH host key verification. Any user may set it; use it only for tests. It is flagged ("Verification disabled") in the instance list and Shuttle logs a warning at start.
- `linux_user`: the Linux user that runs the service; used in the systemd unit of the instance. Empty: the unit contains `User=CHANGE_ME` to replace by hand. Ignored for Windows architectures.
- `built_version`: Shuttle version of the last successful build, shown next to the download button (empty: not built yet). The active `GitInstance` version may be newer; the next download then rebuilds. `last_build`, `last_update`: set by the system.

Warnings shown in the instance list: "Verification disabled" (`insecure`) and "No host key" (SFTP without `host_key`: trust on first use).

Download and installation:
- Downloading compiles the executable from the active `GitInstance` (slow on first download or after changes); deleting also removes the build files.
- The download is the bare executable, or a zip when a certificate (WebDAV or ChemAssistent), a converter, or Windows XP + SFTP (with WinSCP) applies. Every zip contains `INSTALL.txt` with the install steps for the instance: install folder `C:\Program Files\Shuttle` (Windows, plus `shuttle_task.vbs` in `shell:startup`) or `/opt/Shuttle` (Linux), working folder and log (`shuttle_log.txt`), the sent register (`sent_register.json`; the first start sends every stable file in `src` once) and `known_hosts`. `INSTALL.txt` contains no secrets.
- Linux: the instance list has a "systemd unit" button (per-instance `shuttle.service`, owner/staff only); install it as `/etc/systemd/system/shuttle.service`, then `systemctl daemon-reload` and `systemctl enable --now shuttle.service`. A generic unit without user exists for old links.
- Listed in `<shuttle-instance-list>`, created/edited/copied in `<shuttle-instance-edit>`.

models.name: SdcUser
models.doc:
A user account of the site (the project's Django user model); one record per person who can log in.

- `username` (unique, used to log in), `first_name`, `last_name`, `email`; `is_staff`, `is_superuser`,
  `is_active`, `groups`, `date_joined`, `last_login` as in Django's standard user.
- `email_confirmed`: `true` once the user followed the link in the confirmation e-mail (`<sdc-confirm-email>`).
- The password is never sent to the client; it is changed with the `password_form` (`<sdc-change-password>`)
  or reset by e-mail (`<sdc-password-forgotten>`).
- Anyone may create an account (registration in `<register>`). By default a logged-in user can read and
  edit only their own record (`username`, names, `email`); superusers can see and edit all users, and only
  superusers may delete users.
- Saving a new or changed `email` resets `email_confirmed` to `false` and sends a confirmation e-mail to
  that address (link valid for 3 days).
- Edited in `<sdc-model-form>` via the "Edit <username>" link of `<sdc-user-nav-btn>`; `<sdc-user>` loads
  the current user's record.

tasks.title: Register a new account
steps: Fill `username`, `password1` and `password2` (the user types the passwords) and optionally the names and `email`.
The user clicks "Create"; with an `email` a confirmation e-mail is sent.
